title: Essential Barbell
author: Iron And Sand
desc:
Essential Barbell is a two-week strength training programme aimed at both novice and intermediate lifters. It is built around the seven fundamental movement patterns:
Squat
Hinge
Horizontal Press
Vertical Press
Horizontal Pull
Vertical Pull
Downward Press

There are no gimmicks. No unnecessary variations. Just put plates on the bar and lift.
Then do it again.
And again.
And again.
That's how strength is forged and muscle grown.

The programme consists of three workouts per week, ideally performed with a rest day between each session (for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday).

Week 1

Workout 1
Squat
Bench Press
Barbell Row

Workout 2
Overhead Press
Deadlift
Bodyweight Dips

Workout 3
Squat
Bench Press
Bodyweight Pull-ups

Week 2

Workout 1
Squat
Overhead Press
Dumbbell Row

Workout 2
Bench Press
Deadlift
Weighted Dips

Workout 3
Squat
Overhead Press
Weighted Pull-ups

All barbell and weighted lifts are performed for 3 sets of 5 reps.  Once you can complete all three sets of five with good technique, increase the weight at your next session and build back up again if necessary.

Bodyweight pull-ups and dips are performed for 3 AMRAP (As Many Reps As Possible) sets. 

Before each main lift, perform enough warm-up sets to prepare for your working weight. Begin with the empty bar where appropriate, then gradually add weight while reducing the number of repetitions as you approach your working sets.
For example:
Empty bar (20kg) - 1x10.
40kg - 1x8.
60kg - 1x6.
80kg - 3x5.

At the end of each two-week cycle, simply return to Week 1. Progression is built into the programme through the consistent increase in weight over time. In this way, Essential Barbell provides a simple framework that can support years of strength training.

ex.note:
Preferably use overhand or neutral grip as this will increase lat engagement. Underarm 'chins' will focus on biceps.
If you want to you can rotate the grip you use, every 6 weeks or so.
If you don't have a dipping belt you can suspend weight plates, kettlebells or a dumbbell from a tight resistance band. Its unwieldy but it works. You can also use a small rucksack or weighted vest.
